title: Failure Boundary Explorer
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Learning Record Store
Operations
Failure Modes
Durability
description: Break one component of the full LRS at a time and see why only a failure before the durability boundary at Kafka can lose data, while every failure after it only degrades freshness or speed.
audience: Teachers, instructional designers, learning-technology developers and learning-analytics practitioners (college undergraduate and professional development)

educational.topic: Full LRS failure modes and the durability boundary
learningObjectives: The learner will differentiate the one failure that can lose data from the failures that only degrade freshness or speed, by locating each failing component relative to the durability boundary at Kafka.

accessibility.notes: The failure select and Restore button are keyboard operable and the panel is an aria-live region; node clicks need a pointer, but every component is also reachable through the select.

controls.label: Restore all
controls.action: Restore every component and show the running findings

controls.label: Click a component
controls.action: Show its role and whether it is built or designed

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Predict, break one component, compare against the durability rule
keyQuestions: Which single failure can lose data, and why?
Why does a failure after Kafka heal on recovery?
Why is a gateway failure safe only if producers retry?
commonMisconceptions: That losing the database of record (ClickHouse) loses data
That the gateway holds statements it has not yet queued
assessmentOpportunities: Sort the components before and after testing

simulation.modelType: static architecture diagram with scripted failure states
assumptions: Status labels follow the repository TODO dated 2026-09-26 as quoted in Chapters 20-21
Detection mechanisms are described generically where the chapter does not specify them
limitations: Shows one failure at a time; combined failures and the vault/identity service are not modelled
